correctness.rationale: The two fluctuation eigenspaces have eigenvalues δx and ε; the normalized block means give Q(x) with diagonal rx,s and squared off-diagonal mn a²x. Q is positive definite and its top eigenvalue exceeds both fluctuation levels. Any positive diagonal congruence with condition number k produces H=λ_min(DAD)D⁻² satisfying H≼A≼kH, and feasibility implies condition number at most k in the reverse direction. Averaging H under block permutations preserves feasibility. At optimal k the averaged scaling must attain both spectral bounds 1 and k. Its upper PSD slack has a strictly positive null vector w by Perron–Frobenius; every summand's PSD slack must annihilate w, forcing H equal to its average, since the difference is diagonal. Thus unrestricted optimal scalings cannot break the symmetry. Of the three competing ratios, λ+/λ− decreases then increases about x₀ by the trace divided by square root of determinant; λ+/(δx) strictly decreases and λ+/ε strictly increases by comparing positive Perron matrices Q/x and Q. For x_E≤x₀, δx≥ε throughout the candidate interval, so the competition there is between the decreasing quotient and increasing ε-branch. The sign of det(Q−εI) is the sign of λ−−ε; its affine root is the first claimed crossing if rc>ma², otherwise the quotient dominates. For x_E≥x₀, δx≤ε throughout the candidate interval, and det(Q−δxI)/x is affine decreasing with root (bs−na²)/(b(1−b)). Strict monotonicity outside each interval and the competing monotone branches inside prove both clipping and uniqueness; if x_E=x₀ the interval is a point. In the all-n example the eigenvalues are 1/2 and (n+2)/2 on the quotient and 3/4 and 1/2 on fluctuations at x=5/6; at n=3,x=1 the least eigenvalue is 1/2 and the largest is (16+√106)/10. All strict hypotheses hold in these checks.
residual_risks: The packaged finite exact and numerical checks were not rerun. The independent analytic check applies to the strict positivity and SPD domain only.

value.rationale: Two exchangeable communities are a natural correlation model. A closed-form rule determines when each of two different within-community fluctuation levels, rather than quotient balancing, sets the optimum. It removes any entrywise optimization and establishes that a nonsymmetric diagonal cannot tie it. The fixed-ratio all-size example and the strict Jacobi gap illustrate directly why unit diagonal does not suffice. This is useful as an exact benchmark for general preconditioning, not merely a numerical improvement on one selected matrix.
residual_risks: The result concerns spectral condition numbers for this strict family. It does not establish gains in iteration counts or floating-point behavior.
